newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Creditanstalt launches Romania market indices.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt launches Romania market indices.

text.p: Romania-based Creditanstalt Securities said on Tuesday it had launched indices for the Bucharest bourse and the Romanian over-the-counter (OTC) market.

"These indices will be used to forecast market trends and make investment recommendations to our clients," company executive president Marcel Cobuz told Reuters. Creditanstalt Securities is the brokerage arm of Austria's Creditanstalt Investment Bank (CAIB).
Neither the Bucharest stock exchange nor the OTC system has any official guage of market movements. Exchange general manager Stere Farmache said the bourse would publish an index within a month.
The new indices are market-value-weighted and computed after each session on the basis of moves in average prices and the capitalisation of listed stocks. Their currency base is Romania's leu.
Creditanstalt's CAS-SE index for the bourse, with a 1,000-point base set in January 1996, considers all 41 listed stocks.
The CAS-RQ for the RASDAQ Romanian OTC system has a base of 100 points, set this January. It considers the 50 most heavily traded stocks on the market.

Cobuz said the new indices were part of a CAIB campaign to promote Romania. It has published a market report outlining companies and industrial sectors, as well as political and macro-economic prospects until the turn of the century.
Creditanstalt plans to launch soon the same indices using the dollar as a base for computation, he added.
The indices will be displayed on CASE02.
